brief:
Today, Friday 25 September, is a rest day. You trained six days in a row, 19 to 24 September, and your plan runs six on, one off. No lifting today.

Last night's Legs B was done exactly as written, every set and every rep. That closes the week's heavy-leg work cleanly.

Tomorrow, Saturday 26 September, is Push A, still a light deload night. Tomorrow morning's review will set its numbers. The deload ends Sunday 27 September and Meso 3 starts Monday 28 September.

Looking ahead to Meso 3 on Push A: the chest press is the one lift that has earned a step. On 19 September you did 12 reps, the top of the range, on every set. That was before Warsaw, so the step will be worked out on the Warsaw machine, not copied across. The shoulder press has sat at 45 for 9 on two visits, and the overhead triceps and rope pushdown have slipped a rep or two. Those are the lifts to watch.

Use today. Step on a scale: nobody has weighed you since 23 August (207 lb, 33 days ago) and the show is 157 days out. A 20-minute easy walk counts as cardio, and your log holds one cardio session ever.

flags.note: Rest day today. Six sessions ran 19 to 24 September. Tomorrow is Push A.
Deload week, day 5 of 7. Deload ends Sunday 27 September; Meso 3 starts Monday 28 September.
No bodyweight since 23 August, 207 lb, 33 days ago. The show is 157 days out.
Your log holds one cardio session ever, 15 minutes on 21 July. Nothing logged this month.
Last night's two cable crunch sets were saved 48 minutes apart (15:21 and 16:09 UTC). That gap is why the session reads 69 minutes; everything before it took about 20.
The second face-pull set from Pull A on 20 September was saved on 21 September, about 27 hours later, so it was typed in afterwards.

The Pull A row slot is named Seated Cable Row (wide), but you wrote 'One armed dumbbell row' on 10 September and logged it in kilograms on 20 September. The per-gym slot swap in your settings is where that name lives.
Your recovery trainer read every note from 19 to 24 September by hand. No pain, tweak or soreness anywhere.
All three trainers reported. All held on tomorrow's lifts, so there were no disagreements and no vetoes. One Yes/No card carries over: the shrug rep range.

proposals.why: You wrote "35kg is heaviest dumbbell" on 15 September and then shrugged it for fifteen reps on all three sets — the top of the range — the same fifteens you hit on 3 September. The weight has nowhere to go and neither do the reps, so this lift has no way to get harder in Meso 3. This opens the top of the range to twenty reps. The bottom stays at twelve, so nothing else about the slot changes.
